title: Minimum of Three Without Comparisons
statement:
You are given `t` test cases. Each test case consists of three integers `a`, `b` and `c`. For each test case, print the smallest of the three numbers.

The interview version of this problem forbids comparison operators: you may not use `<`, `>`, `<=`, `>=`, `==`, `!=`, built-in `min` or `max`, sorting, or conditionals that depend on comparing the numbers. Arithmetic and bitwise operations are allowed, for example a sign-bit trick on the difference of two numbers.

**Follow-up:** the judge can only check the printed answers, so the no-comparison rule is not enforced here. Try to honour it anyway: the point of the exercise is to derive the minimum of two numbers from the sign of their difference.
inputFormat:
The first line contains an integer `t`.
Each of the next `t` lines contains three integers `a`, `b` and `c`.
outputFormat: Print `t` lines: the minimum of each triple.

examples.explanation: The smallest of 4, 9, 2 is 2. In the second case two values tie at -5, which is smaller than 7. In the third case all values are equal.
The extreme values still fit: the difference of two inputs is at most 2·10^9 in magnitude, so use a 64-bit type when working with differences.

hints: Reduce the problem to the minimum of two numbers, then apply it twice: min(a, b, c) = min(min(a, b), c).
The sign of d = a - b tells which one is smaller. Shifting d right arithmetically gives -1 (all ones) when d is negative and 0 otherwise.
min(a, b) = b + (d AND (d >> 63)) for d = a - b in 64-bit arithmetic: when a < b the mask keeps d and the result is a; otherwise the mask is 0 and the result is b.
